curation.notes: AFM force-spectroscopy indentation of free-standing pore-spanning lipid bilayers mimicking plasma-membrane composition (cholesterol, sphingomyelin varied); breakthrough force, pre-stress and elasticity extracted with a clamped-membrane point-load model. Membrane-level (not single-molecule) measurement; FGF2 adsorption studied by AFM imaging only.

evidence.snippet: All experiments were performed at room temperature (controlled at ca. 20 °C).
MSNL-D probes (silicon nitride, spring constant 0.03 N m−1, resonance frequency 15 kHz, nominal tip radius 2 nm) were used for indentation experiments

entities.name: Pore-spanning lipid bilayer of plasma-membrane-mimicking composition (with/without cholesterol and sphingomyelin)

evidence.snippet: In this study, we prepare pore-spanning membranes that mimic the composition of plasma membranes and perform force spectroscopy indentation measurements to unravel mechanistic insights depending on lipid composition.
we investigate the adsorption and movement of a peripheral protein, the fibroblast growth factor 2, on the complex membrane.
